questions.prompt: What is the embryo inside a seed?
options: The tiny baby plant that can grow into a new plant
A store of green food only
A flower that has already bloomed
questions.explanation: The embryo is the actual baby plant tucked inside the seed, ready to grow when the conditions are right.
questions.misconception: Some learners think the seed shell or the stored food is the plant. The embryo is the live baby plant; the rest protects and feeds it.

questions.prompt: What does the seed coat do?
questions.explanation: The tough seed coat protects the embryo and stored food from damage while the seed waits for the right moment to germinate.
questions.misconception: The seed coat is not for eating or flowering - it is a protective outer layer around the embryo and food.

questions.prompt: Why does a seed contain stored food?
options: To give the new seedling its first energy before it has leaves
To make the seed turn blue
questions.explanation: The stored food feeds the germinating seedling until it grows its first leaves and can make its own food by photosynthesis.
questions.misconception: The food isn't for people or birds; it is a reserve that powers the young plant before it can photosynthesize.

questions.prompt: What does a seed need so it can germinate?
questions.explanation: A seed germinates when it gets the right water, warmth, and air, so the embryo can start to grow into a new plant.
questions.misconception: Some learners think a seed just needs sunlight to start. Actually it must first take in water and have warmth and air to germinate.
